rows.note: This is the all-purpose verb for optimistically wanting or expecting something to happen or to obtain something.

example.english: I hope it won't rain tomorrow.
example.jyutping: ngo5 hei1 mong6 ting1 jat6 m4 hou2 lok6 jyu5

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for the feeling that something desired may happen.

example.english: We lost the first match, but we still have hope of qualifying.
example.traditional: 輸咗第一場，我哋仲有希望出線。
example.jyutping: syu1 zo2 dai6 jat1 coeng4 ngo5 dei6 zung6 jau5 hei1 mong6 ceot1 sin3

rows.note: Use this for hope placed in a person or thing, especially in expressions such as 冇指望.

example.english: With the captain out, this team really has no hope today.
example.traditional: 呢隊波今場冇咗隊長，真係冇指望。
example.jyutping: ni1 deoi6 bo1 gam1 coeng4 mou5 zo2 deoi6 zoeng2 zan1 hai6 mou5 zi2 mong6

rows.note: Use this in written or formal contexts for a strong, expectant hope or longing.

example.english: Citizens hope the government will announce the result soon.
example.traditional: 市民盼望政府盡快公布結果。
example.jyutping: si5 man4 paan3 mong6 zing3 fu2 zeon6 faai3 gung1 bou3 git3 gwo2
